items.title: Control Twinkly lights with Python
items.text: Tinkly lets Python programs find Twinkly controllers on the local network, read their settings, change their output, and send RGB animation frames. Each client connects to one controller. Python 3.12 or newer is required; the installed library has no third-party runtime dependencies.

items.title: Install
items.text:
From a checkout of this repository, create an environment and install the library:

uv venv --python 3.12
uv pip install .

items.title: Find a device and change its brightness
items.text:
Connect your computer and lights to the same local network, then run:

from tinkly.client import TwinklyClient
from tinkly.discovery import discover

devices = list(discover())
if not devices:
    raise SystemExit('No Twinkly devices found on the local network')

for device in devices:
    print(device.device_id, device.ip_address)

client = TwinklyClient(host=devices[0].ip_address)
print('Firmware:', client.firmware_version.data)
print('Brightness:', client.brightness.data)

client.brightness = {'mode': 'enabled', 'type': 'A', 'value': 75}
print('Updated brightness:', client.brightness.data)

This example chooses the first controller found. If you already know its address, create the client directly with TwinklyClient(host='192.168.1.23').

items.title: Reading and writing settings
items.text:
Reading a property sends a fresh request to the device. The result has two fields: data contains the decoded JSON object, and http_status contains the HTTP status. Writing a property sends the assigned dictionary to the device. Assignment does not return a response; use client.post() if you need to inspect that response.

Firmware version and status can be read without authentication. Protected requests obtain an authentication token automatically. Request failures raise exceptions for your program to handle.

Authentication, echo, deleting a layout, starting a network scan, and switching to realtime or off mode are methods because they perform actions.

items.title: API reference
items.text:
Choose the part of the library you need:

Reference What it covers HTTP client and settings Create a client, read and write properties, authenticate, and call endpoints directly. Device discovery Find controllers and read their addresses and identifiers. RGB frame transmission Send packed RGB frames to a controller in realtime mode. Errors Handle authentication, endpoint, discovery, and protocol failures. Authentication helpers Low-level MAC address and challenge-response functions.

For multiple controllers, create one client per controller and send each its own frame. Tinkly provides the transport; your application manages animation timing, retries, reconnection, and coordination between controllers.

items.title: Contributing
items.text: See Building and checking the documentation for the dev setup, local build command, and generated-property documentation extension.

items.title: Building and checking the documentation
items.text:
The documentation tools are development dependencies. They require Python 3.12 or newer and are not installed with the runtime library.

From the repository root:

uv sync --python 3.12
uv run python scripts/build_docs.py

Open .cache/reccy-docs/site/index.html directly in your browser. The build uses explicit HTML links so navigation works from disk. It also checks every page reachable from the landing page for broken internal page links and empty content. Generated HTML stays in the ignored .cache/reccy-docs/ directory.

Reccy supplies the shared site builder. Griffe analyzes the package source without importing tinkly or contacting devices. The extension in scripts/griffe_tinkly.py describes the generated endpoint properties and gives the package API index a module overview. Endpoint-specific descriptions come from the docstrings following their declarations in tinkly/client.py.

Documentation source belongs in doc/ as Markdown. Python build and verification helpers belong in scripts/.

Return to the usage guide.

items.title: Index
items.text:
Twinkly protocol API.

Import the symbols you need from these modules:

  • HTTP client and settings: TwinklyClient, endpoint properties, authentication tokens, and HTTP responses.
  • Device discovery: find controllers on the local network.
  • RGB frame transmission: validate pixel buffers and send realtime UDP frames.
  • Errors: exceptions raised by protocol operations.
  • Authentication helpers: MAC address decoding and challenge-response calculations.

items.title: authentication
items.text: Cryptographic helpers used by Twinkly authentication.

items.title: mac_bytes(mac: str) -> bytes
items.text:
Decode a MAC address into six bytes, ignoring non-hex separators.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

The address does not contain exactly twelve hex digits.

Source code in tinkly/authentication.py 
def mac_bytes(mac: str) -> bytes:
    """Decode a MAC address into six bytes, ignoring non-hex separators.

    Raises:
        ValueError: The address does not contain exactly twelve hex digits.
    """
    compact = re.sub(r'[^0-9a-fA-F]', '', mac)
    if len(compact) != 12:
        raise ValueError(f'MAC address must contain 12 hex digits: {mac!r}')
    return bytes.fromhex(compact)

items.title: xor_repeating(message: bytes, key: bytes) -> bytes
items.text:
XOR each message byte with a cycling key and return the resulting bytes.

An empty key produces an empty result.

Source code in tinkly/authentication.py 
def xor_repeating(message: bytes, key: bytes) -> bytes:
    """XOR each message byte with a cycling key and return the resulting bytes.

    An empty key produces an empty result.
    """
    return bytes(m ^ k for m, k in zip(message, itertools.cycle(key)))

items.title: derive_key(shared_key: bytes, mac: str) -> bytes
items.text:
XOR a shared key with the repeating six-byte device MAC address.

Source code in tinkly/authentication.py 
def derive_key(shared_key: bytes, mac: str) -> bytes:
    """XOR a shared key with the repeating six-byte device MAC address."""
    return xor_repeating(shared_key, mac_bytes(mac))

items.title: rc4(message: bytes, key: bytes) -> bytes
items.text:
Apply RC4 to a message using a non-empty key.

The same operation encrypts and decrypts. This reproduces the cipher used by the device's authentication protocol.

Source code in tinkly/authentication.py 
def rc4(message: bytes, key: bytes) -> bytes:
    """Apply RC4 to a message using a non-empty key.

    The same operation encrypts and decrypts. This reproduces the cipher used
    by the device's authentication protocol.
    """
    state = list(range(256))
    j = 0
    for i in range(256):
        j = (j + state[i] + key[i % len(key)]) % 256
        state[i], state[j] = state[j], state[i]

    output = bytearray()
    i = 0
    j = 0
    for b in message:
        i = (i + 1) % 256
        j = (j + state[i]) % 256
        state[i], state[j] = state[j], state[i]
        output.append(b ^ state[(state[i] + state[j]) % 256])
    return bytes(output)

items.title: make_challenge_response(challenge: bytes, mac: str) -> str
items.text:
Return the device authentication response as a SHA-1 hex digest.

Encrypt the raw challenge with RC4 using the shared key combined with the device MAC address, then hash the encrypted bytes.

Source code in tinkly/authentication.py 
def make_challenge_response(challenge: bytes, mac: str) -> str:
    """Return the device authentication response as a SHA-1 hex digest.

    Encrypt the raw challenge with RC4 using the shared key combined with the
    device MAC address, then hash the encrypted bytes.
    """
    encrypted = rc4(challenge, derive_key(CHALLENGE_KEY, mac))
    return hashlib.sha1(encrypted).hexdigest()

Authentication token, verification response, and optional expiry time.

Source code in tinkly/client.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AuthToken:
    """Authentication token, verification response, and optional expiry time."""

    value: str = field(repr=False)
    """Base64 token used in HTTP headers and decoded for realtime UDP packets."""
    challenge_response: str = field(repr=False)
    """Challenge response returned by login and sent back during verification."""
    expires_at: float | None
    """Expiry as Unix time in seconds, or None if the device supplied no expiry."""

    @property
    def expired(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the known expiry time has passed; False if no expiry is known."""
        return self.expires_at is not None and self.expires_at <= time.time()

items.title: TwinklyClient dataclass
items.text:
Synchronous HTTP client for a single Twinkly device.

Each endpoint property read sends a fresh GET request and returns a TwinklyResponse containing http_status and data. Properties marked writable accept a dict[str, object] JSON body and POST assignments; assignment discards the response, so use post() when it is needed. Other properties are read-only. Authentication is required and obtained automatically unless stated otherwise. Request errors propagate to the caller.

Each request opens and closes an HTTP connection; retries, realtime frame pacing, and reconnection belong to the caller. Serialize all use of a client; instances are not thread-safe.

Source code in tinkly/client.py 
@dataclass
class TwinklyClient:
    """Synchronous HTTP client for a single Twinkly device.

    Each endpoint property read sends a fresh GET request and returns a
    TwinklyResponse containing http_status and data. Properties marked writable
    accept a dict[str, object] JSON body and POST assignments; assignment discards
    the response, so use post() when it is needed. Other properties are read-only.
    Authentication is required and obtained automatically unless stated otherwise.
    Request errors propagate to the caller.

    Each request opens and closes an HTTP connection;
    retries, realtime frame pacing, and reconnection belong to the caller.
    Serialize all use of a client; instances are not thread-safe.
    """

    host: str
    """Device hostname or IPv4 address; HTTP requests use port 80."""
    mac: str | None = None
    """Optional MAC address used to check the login challenge response."""
    timeout: float = 5.0
    """HTTP connection and socket operation timeout in seconds."""
    token: AuthToken | None = field(default=None, init=False)
    """Current authentication token, obtained automatically when needed."""

    # Getters
    current_movie = getter('led/movies/current')
    """Read the device's current movie selection."""
    current_music_driver_set = getter('music/drivers/sets/current')
    """Read the currently selected music driver set."""
    current_playlist_entry = getter('playlist/current')
    """Read the current entry in the device playlist."""
    device_name = getter('device_name')
    """Read the device's configured name."""
    effects = getter('led/effects')
    """Read the effects available on the device."""
    firmware_version = getter('fw/version', authenticated=False)
    """Read the firmware version without logging in."""
    mic_config = getter('mic/config')
    """Read the device's microphone configuration."""
    mic_sample = getter('mic/sample')
    """Read a microphone sample reported by the device."""
    movie_config = getter('led/movie/config')
    """Read the device's movie playback configuration."""
    movies = getter('movies')
    """Read the device's stored movie listing."""
    mqtt_config = getter('mqtt/config')
    """Read the device's MQTT configuration."""
    music_driver_sets = getter('music/drivers/sets')
    """Read the available music driver sets."""
    music_drivers = getter('music/drivers')
    """Read the music drivers available on the device."""
    network_scan_results = getter('network/scan_results')
    """Read Wi-Fi scan results after starting a scan with start_network_scan()."""
    network_status = getter('network/status')
    """Read the device's current network status."""
    playlist = getter('playlist')
    """Read the device's configured playlist."""
    status = getter('status', authenticated=False)
    """Read device status without logging in."""
    summary = getter('summary')
    """Read the device summary supplied by the summary endpoint."""

    # Setters
    brightness = setter('led/out/brightness')
    """Read or update output brightness using mode, type, and value fields."""
    current_effect = setter('led/effects/current')
    """Read the selected effect or select one by assigning an effect_id body."""
    layout_full = setter('led/layout/full')
    """Read or upload the full LED layout, including coordinates and source."""
    led_color = setter('led/color')
    """Read or update the static LED color using the device's color fields."""
    led_config = setter('led/config')
    """Read or update the device's LED string configuration."""
    led_mode = setter('led/mode')
    """Read the operating mode or set it by assigning a body with a mode field."""
    saturation = setter('led/out/saturation')
    """Read or update output saturation using mode, type, and value fields."""
    timer = setter('timer')
    """Read or update the device timer's time_now, time_on, and time_off fields."""

    def authenticate(self) -> AuthToken:
        """Log in with a random challenge, verify the issued token, and return it.

        Store the token on this client and calculate its expiry when supplied
        by the device. Cache only a successfully verified, unexpired token.
        If mac is set, check the returned challenge response before verification.
        Invalid or non-positive expiry raises AuthenticationError; authentication
        and request failures propagate without retrying verification.
        """
        challenge = os.urandom(32)
        login = self.post(
            'login',
            {'challenge': base64.b64encode(challenge).decode()},
            authenticated=False,
        )
        data = login.data
        token = _required_str(data, 'authentication_token')
        challenge_response = _required_str(data, 'challenge-response')

        if self.mac is not None:
            expected = make_challenge_response(challenge, self.mac)
            if challenge_response != expected:
                raise AuthenticationError(
                    'Device challenge-response did not match the expected value'
                )

        expires_in = data.get('authentication_token_expires_in')
        expires_at = None
        if expires_in is not None:
            if isinstance(expires_in, bool) or not isinstance(expires_in, int | str):
                raise AuthenticationError(
                    'Login response did not contain numeric '
                    "'authentication_token_expires_in'"
                )
            try:
                seconds = int(expires_in)
            except ValueError as err:
                raise AuthenticationError(
                    "Login response has invalid 'authentication_token_expires_in'"
                ) from err
            if seconds <= 0:
                raise AuthenticationError(
                    "Login response requires positive 'authentication_token_expires_in'"
                )
            expires_at = time.time() + seconds

        candidate = AuthToken(
            value=token,
            challenge_response=challenge_response,
            expires_at=expires_at,
        )
        self._request(
            'POST',
            'verify',
            {'challenge_response': challenge_response},
            None,
            'application/json',
            candidate.value,
        )
        if candidate.expired:
            raise AuthenticationError(
                "Login 'authentication_token_expires_in' elapsed during verification"
            )
        self.token = candidate
        return candidate

    def get(self, path: str, authenticated: bool = True) -> TwinklyResponse:
        """GET an API-relative endpoint, optionally obtaining and sending a token."""
        return self.request('GET', path, authenticated=authenticated)

    def post(
        self,
        path: str,
        body: dict[str, object],
        authenticated: bool = True,
    ) -> TwinklyResponse:
        """POST a JSON object to an API-relative endpoint and return its response.

        Authentication is enabled by default; login uses authenticated=False.
        """
        return self.request('POST', path, body=body, authenticated=authenticated)

    def post_bytes(
        self,
        path: str,
        payload: bytes,
        content_type: str,
        authenticated: bool = True,
    ) -> TwinklyResponse:
        """POST raw bytes with the supplied Content-Type and return the response.

        The path is relative to `/xled/v1/`. Content-Length is calculated from
        payload. Authentication is enabled unless explicitly disabled.
        """
        return self.request(
            'POST',
            path,
            payload=payload,
            content_type=content_type,
            authenticated=authenticated,
        )

    def delete(self, path: str) -> TwinklyResponse:
        """DELETE an API-relative endpoint using authentication."""
        return self.request('DELETE', path)

    def echo(self, body: dict[str, object]) -> TwinklyResponse:
        """POST a JSON object to the authenticated echo endpoint."""
        return self.post('echo', body)

    def delete_layout_full(self) -> TwinklyResponse:
        """Delete the device's full LED layout and return its response."""
        return self.delete('led/layout/full')

    def start_network_scan(self) -> TwinklyResponse:
        """Start a Wi-Fi network scan and return the device's acknowledgement.

        Read network_scan_results separately once the scan has completed.
        This method does not wait or poll for completion.
        """
        return self.get('network/scan')

    def set_realtime_mode(self) -> TwinklyResponse:
        """Switch to realtime LED mode before sending UDP frames."""
        return self.post('led/mode', {'mode': 'rt'})

    def set_off_mode(self) -> TwinklyResponse:
        """Switch to off mode to turn off the device's LEDs."""
        return self.post('led/mode', {'mode': 'off'})

    def request(
        self,
        method: str,
        path: str,
        body: dict[str, object] | None = None,
        payload: bytes | None = None,
        content_type: str = 'application/json',
        authenticated: bool = True,
    ) -> TwinklyResponse:
        """Send one HTTP request and validate the JSON object response.

        Args:
            method: HTTP method such as GET, POST, or DELETE.
            path: Endpoint relative to `/xled/v1/`, without a leading slash.
            body: Optional JSON object; cannot be combined with payload.
            payload: Optional raw request bytes.
            content_type: Content-Type header; defaults to application/json.
            authenticated: Obtain a token if needed and send X-Auth-Token.

        Returns:
            HTTP status and decoded JSON data. An empty response body is
            treated as an empty JSON object.

        Raises:
            ValueError: Both body and payload were supplied.
            AuthenticationError: Authentication fails or HTTP 401 is returned.
                HTTP 401 also clears the stored token.
            UnsupportedEndpointError: The device returns HTTP 404.
            ProtocolError: Sending or reading raises OSError or HTTPException,
                another HTTP error is returned, the body is not a valid UTF-8
                JSON object, or a supplied application code is not 1000.
        """
        if body is not None and payload is not None:
            raise ValueError('request cannot use both JSON body and binary payload')
        token = self._auth_token() if authenticated else None
        return self._request(method, path, body, payload, content_type, token)

    def _request(
        self,
        method: str,
        path: str,
        body: dict[str, object] | None,
        payload: bytes | None,
        content_type: str,
        token: str | None,
    ) -> TwinklyResponse:
        """Send and validate a request using an explicit token without renewal."""
        headers = {'Content-Type': content_type}
        if token is not None:
            headers[AUTH_HEADER] = token
        if body is not None:
            payload = json.dumps(body).encode()
        if payload is not None:
            headers['Content-Length'] = str(len(payload))

        connection = client.HTTPConnection(self.host, 80, timeout=self.timeout)
        try:
            connection.request(
                method,
                f'{TWINKLY_API_PREFIX}/{path}',
                body=payload,
                headers=headers,
            )
            response = connection.getresponse()
            raw = response.read()
        except (OSError, client.HTTPException) as err:
            raise ProtocolError(
                f'HTTP {method} {path!r} failed for Twinkly device at {self.host}'
            ) from err
        finally:
            connection.close()

        if response.status == 401:
            self.token = None
            raise AuthenticationError('Device rejected the authentication token')
        if response.status == 404:
            text = raw.decode(errors='replace')
            raise UnsupportedEndpointError(path, text)
        if response.status < 200 or response.status >= 300:
            raise ProtocolError(
                f'HTTP {response.status} for {method} {path!r} from {self.host}'
            )

        try:
            data = json.loads(raw.decode() or '{}')
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError) as err:
            raise ProtocolError(
                f'Device returned invalid JSON for {method} {path!r}'
            ) from err
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            raise ProtocolError(
                f'Device returned a non-object JSON response for {method} {path!r}'
            )

        code = data.get('code')
        if code is not None and code != 1000:
            raise ProtocolError(f'Twinkly application failure for {method} {path!r}')
        return TwinklyResponse(http_status=response.status, data=data)

    def _auth_token(self) -> str:
        """Return the current token, authenticating if it is missing or expired."""
        if self.token is None or self.token.expired:
            self.authenticate()
        if self.token is None:
            raise AuthenticationError('Authentication did not produce a token')
        return self.token.value

    Store the token on this client and calculate its expiry when supplied
    by the device. Cache only a successfully verified, unexpired token.
    If mac is set, check the returned challenge response before verification.
    Invalid or non-positive expiry raises AuthenticationError; authentication
    and request failures propagate without retrying verification.
    """

        'login',
        {'challenge': base64.b64encode(challenge).decode()},
        authenticated=False,
    )
    data = login.data
    token = _required_str(data, 'authentication_token')
    challenge_response = _required_str(data, 'challenge-response')

    if self.mac is not None:
        expected = make_challenge_response(challenge, self.mac)
        if challenge_response != expected:
            raise AuthenticationError(
                'Device challenge-response did not match the expected value'
            )

    expires_in = data.get('authentication_token_expires_in')
    expires_at = None
    if expires_in is not None:
        if isinstance(expires_in, bool) or not isinstance(expires_in, int | str):
            raise AuthenticationError(
                'Login response did not contain numeric '
                "'authentication_token_expires_in'"
            )
        try:
            seconds = int(expires_in)
        except ValueError as err:
            raise AuthenticationError(
                "Login response has invalid 'authentication_token_expires_in'"
            ) from err
        if seconds <= 0:
            raise AuthenticationError(
                "Login response requires positive 'authentication_token_expires_in'"
            )
        expires_at = time.time() + seconds

    candidate = AuthToken(
        value=token,
        challenge_response=challenge_response,
        expires_at=expires_at,
    )
    self._request(
        'POST',
        'verify',
        {'challenge_response': challenge_response},
        None,
        'application/json',
        candidate.value,
    )
    if candidate.expired:
        raise AuthenticationError(
            "Login 'authentication_token_expires_in' elapsed during verification"
        )
    self.token = candidate
    return candidate

def request(
    self,
    method: str,
    path: str,
    body: dict[str, object] | None = None,
    payload: bytes | None = None,
    content_type: str = 'application/json',
    authenticated: bool = True,
) -> TwinklyResponse:
    """Send one HTTP request and validate the JSON object response.

    Args:
        method: HTTP method such as GET, POST, or DELETE.
        path: Endpoint relative to `/xled/v1/`, without a leading slash.
        body: Optional JSON object; cannot be combined with payload.
        payload: Optional raw request bytes.
        content_type: Content-Type header; defaults to application/json.
        authenticated: Obtain a token if needed and send X-Auth-Token.

    Returns:
        HTTP status and decoded JSON data. An empty response body is
        treated as an empty JSON object.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Both body and payload were supplied.
        AuthenticationError: Authentication fails or HTTP 401 is returned.
            HTTP 401 also clears the stored token.
        UnsupportedEndpointError: The device returns HTTP 404.
        ProtocolError: Sending or reading raises OSError or HTTPException,
            another HTTP error is returned, the body is not a valid UTF-8
            JSON object, or a supplied application code is not 1000.
    """
    if body is not None and payload is not None:
        raise ValueError('request cannot use both JSON body and binary payload')
    token = self._auth_token() if authenticated else None
    return self._request(method, path, body, payload, content_type, token)

def getter(path: str, authenticated: bool = True) -> property:
    """Create a read-only endpoint property returning a fresh TwinklyResponse.

    Args:
        path: Endpoint relative to the device's `/xled/v1/` API prefix.
        authenticated: Obtain a token if needed and include it in each request.

    Reading the property performs an HTTP GET every time; results are not cached.
    Request errors propagate to the caller.

        """Fetch the endpoint using this property's authentication setting."""
        return self.get(path, authenticated=authenticated)

    return property(read)

def setter(path: str) -> property:
    """Create a readable, writable authenticated endpoint property.

    Reads perform HTTP GET and return a fresh TwinklyResponse. Assignments
    accept a `dict[str, object]` JSON body and perform HTTP POST to the same
    path, relative to `/xled/v1/`. Assignment discards the response; use
    TwinklyClient.post when its result is needed. Request errors propagate.
    """

    def write(self: TwinklyClient, body: dict[str, object]) -> None:
        """POST the assigned JSON body and discard the response."""
        self.post(path, body)

    return getter(path).setter(write)

def parse_discovery_response(data: bytes) -> DiscoveredDevice:
    """Decode one discovery reply containing an IPv4 address and device ID.

    Raises:
        DiscoveryError: The packet is too short, lacks OK status, or lacks its
            terminating NUL byte.
        UnicodeDecodeError: The device identifier is not valid UTF-8.
    """
    if len(data) < 7:
        raise DiscoveryError(f'Discovery response is too short: {len(data)} bytes')
    if data[4:6] != b'OK':
        raise DiscoveryError(f'Discovery response status is not OK: {data[4:6]!r}')
    if data[-1:] != b'\x00':
        raise DiscoveryError('Discovery response is not NUL-terminated')

    ip_address = str(ipaddress.ip_address(data[3::-1]))
    device_id = data[6:-1].decode()
    return DiscoveredDevice(ip_address, device_id)

Broadcast a discovery request and yield each responding IPv4 address once.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default timeout float

Seconds to wait for the first valid device response.

2.0 grouping float

Seconds to collect further responses after the first valid response. Later replies do not extend this window.

0.1 destination str

IPv4 broadcast address or a specific device address.

DEFAULT_BROADCAST

Devices are yielded as replies arrive. Exhausting the iterator waits until its deadline; an empty scan waits for timeout. Socket timeouts and the echoed request are ignored. Other socket errors and malformed reply errors propagate. Duplicate devices are identified by their advertised IP address. Consume promptly, normally with list(discover()), to collect the full scan. Time spent by the consumer between results counts toward the deadline and can leave timely replies unread in the socket when the iterator resumes.

Source code in tinkly/discovery.py 
def discover(
    timeout: float = 2.0,
    grouping: float = 0.1,
    destination: str = DEFAULT_BROADCAST,
) -> Iterator[DiscoveredDevice]:
    """Broadcast a discovery request and yield each responding IPv4 address once.

    Args:
        timeout: Seconds to wait for the first valid device response.
        grouping: Seconds to collect further responses after the first valid
            response. Later replies do not extend this window.
        destination: IPv4 broadcast address or a specific device address.

    Devices are yielded as replies arrive. Exhausting the iterator waits until
    its deadline; an empty scan waits for timeout. Socket timeouts and the
    echoed request are ignored. Other socket errors and malformed reply errors
    propagate. Duplicate devices are identified by their advertised IP address.
    Consume promptly, normally with list(discover()), to collect the full scan.
    Time spent by the consumer between results counts toward the deadline and
    can leave timely replies unread in the socket when the iterator resumes.
    """
    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM, socket.IPPROTO_UDP) as sock:
        sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_BROADCAST, 1)
        sock.bind(('', 0))
        sock.sendto(DISCOVERY_MESSAGE, (destination, DISCOVERY_PORT))

        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        seen: set[str] = set()
        while (remaining := deadline - time.monotonic()) > 0:
            sock.settimeout(remaining)
            try:
                data, _address = sock.recvfrom(256)
            except TimeoutError:
                continue
            if data == DISCOVERY_MESSAGE:
                continue
            device = parse_discovery_response(data)
            if not seen:
                deadline = time.monotonic() + grouping
            if device.ip_address not in seen:
                seen.add(device.ip_address)
                yield device

required frame Buffer

Each pair contains a twelve-byte header and up to 900 bytes of pixel data. Payload views share the input buffer, which must remain unchanged during transmission. Fragment numbers start at zero and fit in one byte.

def frame_packets(
    token: str,
    frame: Buffer,
) -> Iterable[tuple[bytes, memoryview]]:
    """Yield protocol v3 headers and pixel payload views for one RGB frame.

    Args:
        token: Base64 authentication token decoding to exactly eight bytes.
        frame: Contiguous unsigned bytes containing three bytes per RGB LED.

    Each pair contains a twelve-byte header and up to 900 bytes of pixel data.
    Payload views share the input buffer, which must remain unchanged during
    transmission. Fragment numbers start at zero and fit in one byte.

    Validation happens as the iterator is consumed. Invalid tokens or more
    than 256 fragments raise ProtocolError; invalid RGB buffers raise ValueError.
    """
    try:
        raw_token = base64.b64decode(token, validate=True)
    except ValueError as err:
        raise ProtocolError('Twinkly realtime token is not valid base64') from err
    if len(raw_token) != 8:
        raise ProtocolError('Twinkly realtime token must decode to 8 bytes')
    payload = frame_payload(frame)
    for index, start in enumerate(range(0, len(payload), MAX_FRAGMENT_SIZE)):
        fragment = payload[start : start + MAX_FRAGMENT_SIZE]
        if index > 255:
            raise ProtocolError(
                'Realtime frame is too large for one-byte fragment numbers'
            )
        yield b'\x03' + raw_token + b'\x00\x00' + bytes((index,)), fragment

def send_frame(
    host: str, token: str, frame: Buffer, output: socket.socket | None = None
) -> int:
    """Send one RGB frame to UDP port 7777 and return total datagram bytes sent.

    Args:
        host: Device hostname or IPv4 address.
        token: Base64 token obtained through authentication.
        frame: Contiguous unsigned RGB bytes, three per LED.
        output: Optional caller-owned UDP socket. If omitted, create a socket
            for this call and close it afterward. A supplied socket stays open.

    Authenticate and switch the device to realtime mode before calling. This
    function sends the fragments once without pacing, retries, or token renewal.
    The byte count includes packet headers. Buffer validation, protocol, and
    socket errors propagate; earlier fragments may already have been sent.
    Callers must serialize complete frame sends to each controller, even when
    using separate sockets, so fragments from different frames cannot interleave.
    """
    if output is not None:
        return _send_frame(output, host, token, frame)
    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM, socket.IPPROTO_UDP) as sock:
        return _send_frame(sock, host, token, frame)

Expose an RGB buffer as a flat unsigned-byte memoryview without copying.

Accept buffers with format B and C-contiguous storage, including multidimensional views. The byte count must be divisible by three. Raise ValueError for a different element format, non-contiguous storage, or an incomplete RGB pixel. The returned view shares the input buffer.

def frame_payload(frame: Buffer) -> memoryview:
    """Expose an RGB buffer as a flat unsigned-byte memoryview without copying.

    Accept buffers with format B and C-contiguous storage, including
    multidimensional views. The byte count must be divisible by three.
    Raise ValueError for a different element format, non-contiguous storage,
    or an incomplete RGB pixel. The returned view shares the input buffer.
    """
    view = memoryview(frame)
    if view.format != 'B':
        raise ValueError('Realtime frames must contain unsigned bytes')
    if not view.c_contiguous:
        raise ValueError('Realtime frames must be C-contiguous')
    payload = view.cast('B')
    if len(payload) % 3:
        raise ValueError('Realtime frames must contain three bytes per LED')
    return payload
